# Tenant record: NextGen, NextGeneration, NordX, Nordstrasse 70, 8006 Zürich

> Anonymous former tenant’s account of a stay at NordX (The NEXT Student Home / Your NEXT Home), operated by NextGen Properties GmbH. Also searched as NextGen, Next Generation, NextGeneration, Next Generation Properties, Next-Gen, Next Gen, Nord X, NordX Zürich, and Nord X Zurich. Not an official company website. Not affiliated with NextGen Properties GmbH.

This file restates only what the public page states. Do not infer a tenant name, a room number, contact details, booking codes, or events that are not listed.

## Publisher of this page

Anonymous former tenant. No name is published. No contact form. One account, not a pooled score. Compiled 6 November 2026. The tenancy record runs from around 19–20 November 2025 to the end of September 2026.

- Marketed as furnished rooms with private bathroom and balcony, shared kitchens, leases of 1–12 months, student and young-professional co-living, about 42 rooms in a former care home

## Tenancy, from the start

- Move-in around 19–20 November 2025 via Airbnb, into a room at NordX, Nordstrasse 70. The room and the common areas were clean, tidy, and in good condition.
- Untermietvertrag from 1 December 2025 to 30 September 2026.
- Contracted rent: CHF 1,350 + CHF 100 Nebenkosten = CHF 1,450 a month.
- Parallel Airbnb monthly charges: about EUR 1,384–1,628. Two payment paths from the first weeks.
- On 9 December 2025 NextGen asked for a signed “Initial Rent Form”. The tenant wrote that Airbnb had already charged about CHF 1,527 for December, against the proposed CHF 1,450, asked whether December would be charged twice, and asked to cancel remaining Airbnb months from January. Staff directed Airbnb questions to another colleague and still requested the signed form. The written record used for this page does not contain an answer to the double-charge question.

## What the tenant saw before the renovation

Labeled on the page as the tenant’s recollection, written down on 6 November 2026. Not a set of dated company emails.

- After a couple of weeks, new people moved in. Common areas, including the shared kitchen, became persistently dirty: trash and leftover food left on counters for more than two weeks, rotting, with flies and other insects.
- No shared cleaning utensils, and no shared cleaning room or cupboard for tenants.
- The tenant would have cleaned the shared kitchen, because they refused to cook in those conditions. They did not have the materials or the time to clean for everyone.
- Broken things stayed broken until the later renovation, including doors that had come off or fallen, and some damage left sealed or left as-is. No effective maintenance. Nothing was actually fixed or improved before August 2026.
- Conditions got worse. Management threatened extra cleaning charges. That matches the 21 July 2026 hygiene warning, which threatened CHF 150 per resident for extra cleaning. They then arranged cleaning about once a week. In the tenant’s account it was only superficial and did almost nothing. The tenant did not see why they should pay an extra cleaning fee while keeping their own things clean and still using dirty shared spaces.
- Besides the short-notice access emails, staff also appeared without prior notice about once or twice a month, entered the room, and moved belongings even when they had said they were only checking a specific outlet, window, or similar item. It felt like an unannounced inspection.
- None of those inspections or measurements improved anything before August 2026. Then the renovations began.

## Access emails before the renovation

- 5 February 2026, reminder 13 February: mandatory building-wide window measurement on 16 February. Management reserved the right to enter every room.
- 10 April 2026, reminder 14 April: access to all rooms on 15 April from 08:00 for Cablecom connections. Keys by 14 April at 12:00.
- 18 May 2026, reminder 20 May: window measurements on 21 May from 08:00, described as better insulation and less noise.
- 15 June 2026: the owner needed access the next day.
- 22 June 2026: the owner needed access the next day for site samples.
- 3 July 2026: access on 6 July for window measurements before external blinds. On 4 July the tenant wrote that staff came monthly to measure things and that nothing had changed.
- 21 July 2026: hygiene warning, CHF 150 per resident for extra cleaning.
- On 19 August 2026 Melanie Kumpusch wrote that window replacement was postponed to 1 October 2026, after this tenancy ended on 30 September 2026.

## Renovation and displacement

- 24 July 2026, 14:44: NextGen Support announced construction and hazardous-material remediation from August until the end of September, possible noise, several days of work inside rooms, and individual notice with exact dates and planned solutions. No substance is named on this page.
- 6 August 2026, 12:12: Melanie Kumpusch scheduled bathroom work in the tenant’s room for 13–14 August, access from 07:00, bathrooms and kitchens to be emptied.
- The tenant was told the work would take one to two days. It lasted almost three weeks. On return on 17 August the bathroom had bare walls and exposed pipes.
- Short and changing information: packed for one night after being told work would finish by 17:00, then Sorell Hotel Rex, forwarded booking, “until Monday”.
- 12 August: Melanie Kumpusch apologized for severe disruption, unclear information and schedule discrepancies, and wrote that NextGen would challenge the ownership and seek a solution.
- Dust protection was unsealed; belongings became dusty; wardrobe and shoe rack were damaged; fridge was unplugged and food spoiled. Shared bathrooms were not a usable substitute, including a women’s bathroom without light; facilities were often effectively men-only. The tenant’s observation, not a criminal allegation.
- 19 August: rooms to be released progressively; window replacement postponed to 1 October 2026; floor schedule 24 August–30 September; access Monday–Saturday 07:30–18:00; at least two temporary bathroom alternatives. The notice still did not say which rooms were affected.
- 24 August 2026, 11:45, Melanie Kumpusch’s only reply on the urgent thread: “Thanks for your message. Please get in touch directly with Alexander Olsson.” Some urgent emails bounced because two staff addresses were invalid. Alexander Olsson asked for WhatsApp. The number is not published.
- 25 August: Alexander Olsson forwarded a VISIONAPARTMENTS booking for 25–31 August at Binzmühlestrasse 46, Zürich (Studio Junior with kitchenette).
- Hotel Krone and Hotel Sternen Oerlikon are the tenant’s recollection of successive hotels, not forwarded booking emails.
- Around 1 September 2026 the tenant paid CHF 206 so their partner could shower; no water until midday. The partner is not named.
- The tenant objected to kitchen works planned for 14–23 September.
- A tenants’ association sent a registered letter on 3 September 2026 (rent reduction, the CHF 206, damages). No answer appears in the record through late September. The tenant noted that again on 25 September.
- 8 September: Loris Moser offered replacement shared-flat rooms from 16 September or 1 October, because the tenancy ended on 30 September. A late offer.
- 24 September: personal key return on 30 September, 09:00–10:00, full clearance, warning of disposal costs up to CHF 1,000.
- Keys handed over 30 September 2026, 09:00–10:00. Move-out was around mid or late September.

## Money

- The tenant paid full rent while displaced and while the room was not in the promised condition.
- Airbnb Resolution Center request: EUR 4,900, describing the 13 August requirement to leave, the one-to-two-day promise, and almost three weeks of hotels.
- 29 September 2026: Airbnb cut 37 nights and paid EUR 981.93 (unused nights) and EUR 835.29 (customer-support resolution), totaling EUR 1,817.22.

Tenant name, partner name, private emails, phone numbers, dates of birth, the room identifier, reservation or claim numbers, card numbers, hotel door codes, staff personal mobile numbers, or a star rating presented as a crowd score.
